Separate Transformers extract instruction steps and ground object descriptions using interface content and screen position.

notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.
summary: Pretrains ActionBert on user interaction traces to combine visual, linguistic, and UI-structure features. It evaluates the resulting UI representations on tasks including icon classification and description-based component retrieval.

notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains WebGUM offline from demonstrations by jointly tuning an instruction-following language model and a vision encoder over webpage screenshots and HTML. The agent predicts browser actions and is evaluated on MiniWoB, WebShop, and Mind2Web.

publication.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems

name: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies instruction-following agents that observe screenshots and act through a generic mouse-and-keyboard action space, evaluating pixel-based pretraining for GUI tasks on MiniWoB++.

name: MineDreamer: Learning to Follow Instructions via Chain-of-Imagination for Simulated-World Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MineDreamer, a Minecraft agent that imagines stages of an instruction and turns them into keyboard-and-mouse actions in a simulated world.

name: Training a Vision Language Model as Smartphone Assistant
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains a smartphone assistant from sequences of screenshots paired with earlier actions. The model predicts UI-only interactions such as taps and swipes, with evaluation on Android in the Wild.

name: Scaling Instructable Agents Across Many Simulated Worlds
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The setting is simulated 3D environments and video games.
summary: The SIMA project trains agents to follow language instructions in simulated 3D worlds, using images as input and keyboard-and-mouse actions as output.

name: Auto-Formula: Recommend Formulas in Spreadsheets using Contrastive Learning for Table Representations
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Auto-Formula recommends formulas for target spreadsheet cells by adapting formulas from similar spreadsheets within an organization.

name: V-Zen: Efficient GUI Understanding and Precise Grounding With A Novel Multimodal LLM
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The related GUIDE dataset paper remains a separate record; this annotation describes the V-Zen model contribution.
summary: Describes V-Zen, a multimodal GUI model with dual-resolution image encoders for grounding and next-action prediction, fine-tuned using GUIDE interface elements and task sequences.

publication.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024

name: MobileVLM: A Vision-Language Model for Better Intra- and Inter-UI Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileVLM adds two pretraining stages and four UI tasks to learn element detail and relationships between successive screens. Its Mobile3M dataset contains three million Chinese mobile UI pages connected by recorded transition actions.

name: Lightweight Neural App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LiMAC combines a compact Action Transformer with a fine-tuned vision-language model for Android app control. It uses textual goals and histories of screenshots and UI trees to predict actions, with evaluation on two mobile-control datasets.

name: JARVIS-VLA: Post-Training Large-Scale Vision Language Models to Play Visual Games with Keyboards and Mouse
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported tasks are Minecraft gameplay tasks.
summary: Introduces Act from Visual Language Post-Training, a method for agents that follow instructions in Minecraft through visual input and actions, adjacent to interface operation.

name: UITron-Speech: Towards Automated GUI Agents Based on Speech Instructions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UITron-Speech, which predicts GUI actions from spoken instructions and screenshots. It combines synthetic speech data and mixed-modality training with a training-free grounding refinement step.

name: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OmniActor, which shares shallow model layers while separating deeper parameters to train jointly on GUI and embodied interactions. A unified action representation and mixed training data support evaluation in both task families.

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.

name: Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The reported agent evaluations use OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.
summary: Introduces Watch & Learn (W&L), which converts human computer-use videos into UI action trajectories by predicting actions between consecutive screen states.

name: See, Think, Act: Online Shopper Behavior Simulation with VLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study concerns simulated shopper behavior and action prediction.
summary: Studies online shopper action prediction with VLM agents using webpage screenshots, HTML, and action history from OPeRA, trained with SFT and hierarchical RL rewards.

name: SwipeGen: Bridging the Execution Gap in GUI Agents via Human-like Swipe Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SwipeGen for synthesizing varied swipe trajectories and SwipeBench for assessing their execution quality. The study examines how richer control of trajectory, speed, and timing changes GUI agents’ interaction performance.

name: Where Not to Learn: Prior-Aligned Training with Subset-based Attribution Constraints
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v6). GUI-agent click decisions are one of two evaluation settings; the other is image classification.
summary: Proposes training with subset-based attribution constraints so models attend to intended evidence, evaluated on image classification and GUI-agent click decisions.

name: Computer-Using World Model
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents a desktop world model that predicts textual UI changes before synthesizing the next screenshot. It learns from Microsoft Office transitions and is evaluated by letting a frozen agent compare simulated actions before execution.

name: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CowCorpus records interleaved human and agent actions during web navigation and identifies distinct patterns of user intervention. Models trained to anticipate these interventions are integrated into live web agents and assessed in a user study.

name: ProactiveMobile: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Boosting Proactive Intelligence on Mobile Devices
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v4).
summary: ProactiveMobile benchmarks mobile agents on inferring latent user intent from device context and generating executable sequences from a pool of 63 APIs.

name: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: GUI-Libra trains GUI agents with action-aware supervision, a curated reasoning dataset and reinforcement learning adapted to partially verifiable actions across web and mobile tasks.

name: CoME: Empowering Channel-of-Mobile-Experts with Informative Hybrid-Capabilities Reasoning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Channel-of-Mobile-Experts (CoME), a mobile agent with experts for screen summary, subtask planning, action decisions and action functions, trained in stages with InfoGain-Driven DPO (Info-DPO).

name: Agentic Critical Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebShop is one of several evaluation settings; the method targets general language-model agents.
summary: Introduces Agentic Critical Training (ACT), a reinforcement-learning warm-up that teaches general agents to choose expert actions over alternatives, with WebShop among its evaluations.

name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.

name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.

name: GameWorld: Towards Standardized and Verifiable Evaluation of Multimodal Game Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its computer-use interface is evaluated through games, alongside a separate semantic-action interface.
summary: Introduces GameWorld, a browser-game benchmark that evaluates multimodal agents through keyboard and mouse controls or semantic actions using outcome checks.

name: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces CUActSpot to evaluate clicks, drags, drawing and other screen interactions across GUI, text, tables, canvases and natural images. A renderer-based pipeline records geometry and screenshots, then generates matching instructions and action traces for training a grounding model.

name: Beyond Binary: Reframing GUI Critique as Continuous Semantic Alignment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: BBCritic ranks candidate GUI-agent actions through instruction–action alignment, while BBBench evaluates fine-grained ranking with a hierarchical action taxonomy.

name: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OmniGUI evaluates step-level action prediction from interleaved smartphone screenshots, synchronous audio and video. Expert demonstrations carry multimodal-dependency annotations, and initial baselines use native multimodal models as agent proxies to study temporal and audio-related failures.

name: Mobile-Aptus: Confidence-Driven Proactive and Robust Interaction in MLLM-based Mobile-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Mobile-Aptus trains mobile agents to output actions and confidence scores, then corrects confidence bias to guide when they request human help.

name: Learn from Weaknesses: Automated Domain Specialization for Small Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: LearnWeak specializes small computer-use agents by finding domain-specific weaknesses, generating targeted tasks, and training separately for planning and execution errors.

name: MIRAGE: Mobile Agents with Implicit Reasoning and Generative World Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports results on AndroidWorld and AndroidControl.
summary: Introduces MIRAGE, which trains mobile app agents to reason in compact latent states and anticipate future screenshots, reducing generated tokens during action selection.

name: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation method for predicting the next spreadsheet action from a user's action history, using curated action sequences.

name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.

name: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MAG jointly evaluates browser task actions and user-facing guides grounded in screenshots through element marks or pixel coordinates. Its harness covers annotation, live evaluation and joint metrics, with an expert-trajectory-augmented GRPO training study.

name: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces EvoGUI, which derives temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and successor-discrimination probes from recorded GUI trajectories. Its web-derived benchmark isolates transition understanding from the other abilities involved in end-to-end task success.

name: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces State Transition Pretraining, which jointly learns to infer actions from GUI changes and predict future states from current screens and actions. Subsequent instruction-trajectory fine-tuning tests whether these representations transfer to desktop and mobile agent tasks.

name: SkillLens: Visual Skill Cards for Retrieval-Augmented GUI Action Prediction and On-Policy Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported student comparison uses 119 tasks from ten websites absent from training.
summary: Introduces SkillLens visual skill cards for retrieved GUI action guidance and CardDistill for training an action-prediction student that runs without retrieval on website tasks.

name: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a Test-Time Self-Evolving framework for GUI grounding that explores unseen interfaces, reflects on predicted coordinates, and distills those reflections into the model.

name: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces LACL-GUI, a contrastive learning objective that distinguishes trajectory quality within both successful and failed GUI executions. It favors concise successes and uses divergence from successful trajectories to differentiate failures during policy optimization.

name: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The main setting is video-game interaction, with GUI control included as an action mode.
summary: Introduces GameWAM, a model for native game play and GUI control that predicts future visuals and keyboard-mouse actions from synchronized gameplay and GUI trajectories.

name: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MaP unifies GUI-navigation objectives by masking and predicting components of multi-turn trajectories. Role-aware adapters address heterogeneous training data, and evaluations compare the approach with direct task-mixture training across navigation benchmarks.

name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.

name: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents
notes: Main Mind2Web evaluation uses 252 recorded tasks assigned to 20 simulated users, frozen demonstration-derived memory and task-macro step metrics; it is not a live-browser completion test. The main split withholds same-site local experience, and sharing gains shrink when local coverage rises. Mind2Web has no preference channel; preference claims come from separate service and coding settings. User-bound retrieval is not a demonstrated privacy or security guarantee.
summary: ShareMem consolidates reusable experience across users while keeping preference retrieval user-bound; its web evaluation predicts target elements and actions on recorded Mind2Web states.

name: SimTrace: Grounded Multimodal User Trajectories Generation for Online User Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract evaluates SimTrace in an e-commerce setting.
summary: Introduces SimTrace, a framework that generates synthetic multimodal web clickstreams by pairing a computer-use client agent's actions with web observations and user context.

name: ReSAIL: Mitigating Collapse in Iterative Agent Self-Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI action prediction on AITZ is a secondary test; the main experiments use ALFWorld and TextCraft.
summary: Introduces ReSAIL, an augmentation for iterative agent self-distillation that selects informative interaction steps; it also tests GUI-agent action prediction.

name: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
notes: The mobile evaluation uses text UI observations and one fixed instance for each of 116 AndroidWorld task types; three repeats share seed 0. Five agent families use different budgets, with candidate-interface and tool-call granularity changes in some variants. Reported costs use fixed experimental prices, and outcome-selected trace labels are not population failure rates. Faster selection does not imply faster or more reliable task completion.
summary: Evaluates Jev as a bounded action selector inside three AndroidWorld agents and two text-based ALFWorld agents, separating decision savings from task success, recovery and resources per delivered outcome.

name: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). WebShop is one setting among five benchmarks, including simulated environments and realistic applications.
summary: Introduces CoPE, which trains language agents to forecast later actions from earlier histories during RL; WebShop is one of five evaluation benchmarks.

name: Beyond Next-Screen Prediction: The Decision Value of GUI World Models
notes: The matched augmentation experiment measures offline ranking; AndroidWorld task-success comparisons use differently trained evaluators and do not isolate prediction value. A separate web evaluator is trained on Mind2Web, and web results do not uniformly favor direct scoring. The main study concerns one-step selection.
summary: Separates next-screen prediction from action evaluation in GUI lookahead and trains Direct Action Ranking on reference actions, comparing prediction-augmented scoring under matched offline supervision.

name: HobbyLM: A Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Family on a Hobby Budget
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Computer use is one component of a broader model-family report.
summary: Describes HobbyLM, a small model family whose post-trained variants include a computer-use agent and an on-device macOS computer-use adapter.

name: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported speed and accuracy comparison is on AndroidControl.
summary: Introduces GUI-JEPA, a mobile GUI policy that scores candidate actions from screenshot latents in a batched pass without decoding action text.

name: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported interaction savings are measured on MobileGym and CUA-Gym-Hub.
summary: Introduces a two-stage GUI-agent RL framework that selects uncertain action checkpoints and expands rollout length as training progresses.

name: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported results use recorded states from held-out assembly families.
summary: Introduces MAGAR-Bench for GUI-based 3D mechanical assembly decisions and recovery, and MAGAR, a selective correction method for assembly outputs and actions.

name: Visual Token Routing: Learning to keep tokens that matter
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports evaluation on OSWorld, CUA-World, and video-game action prediction.
summary: Introduces Visual Token Routing (VTR), which selects visual tokens from current and earlier screenshots to reduce computer-use agent inference cost while retaining action-relevant information.
